children.text: adyāpi tāṃ kanakacampakadāmagaurīṃ phullāravindavadanāṃ tanuromarājīm
children.translated_text: Even now I think of her, fair as a garland of golden campaka flowers, with a face like a blooming lotus and a fine line of body hair,

children.text: suptotthitāṃ madanavihvalalālasāṅgīṃ vidyāṃ pramādaguṇitām iva cintayāmi ||
children.translated_text: rising from sleep, her limbs languid and yearning from love, like knowledge multiplied by heedlessness.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ śaśimukhīṃ navayauvanāḍhyāṃ pīnastanīṃ punar ahaṃ yadi gaurakāntim
children.translated_text: Even now, if I should again see her moon-faced, rich in fresh youth, full-breasted, and fair in radiance,

children.text: paśyāmi manmathaśarānalapīḍitāṅgīṃ gātrāṇi saṃprati karomi suśītalāni ||
children.translated_text: her body tormented by the fire of <s>Manmatha</s>'s arrows, then at once I would make my own limbs perfectly cooled.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ yadi punaḥ kamalāyatākṣīṃ paśyāmi pīvarapayodharabhārakhinnām
children.translated_text: Even now, if I should again see her lotus-wide eyes, wearied by the weight of her swelling breasts,

children.text: saṃpīḍya bāhuyugalena pibāmi vaktram unmattavan madhukaraḥ kamalaṃ yatheṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: I would press her with my pair of arms and drink her mouth like a maddened bee drinking a lotus at will.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ nidhuvanaklamaniḥsahāṅgīm āpāṇḍugaṇḍapatitālakakuntalālim
children.translated_text: Even now I remember her, her limbs unable to bear the fatigue of lovemaking, a row of loosened curls fallen on her pale cheeks,

children.text: pracchannapāpakṛtamantharam āvahantīṃ kaṇṭhāvasaktabāhulatāṃ smarāmi ||
children.translated_text: moving slowly as though from a hidden sin, with her creeper-like arms fastened around my neck.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ suratajāgaraghūrṇamāna tiryagvalattaralatārakam āyatākṣīm
children.translated_text: Even now at dawn I remember her wide eyes, reeling from the wakefulness of love, with restless pupils glancing sideways,

children.text: śṛṅgārasārakamalākararājahaṃsīṃ vrīḍāvinamravadanām uṣasi smarāmi ||
children.translated_text: a royal swan in the lotus-lake that is the essence of passion, her face bowed with modesty.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ yadi punaḥ śravaṇāyatākṣīṃ paśyāmi dīrghavirahajvaritāṅgayaṣṭim
children.translated_text: Even now, if I should again see her, whose eyes reach to her ears, her slender body fevered by long separation,

children.text: aṅgair ahaṃ samupaguhya tato 'tigāḍhaṃ nonmīlayāmi nayane na ca tāṃ tyajāmi ||
children.translated_text: then, embracing her very tightly with my limbs, I would not open my eyes, nor would I let her go.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ suratatāṇḍavasūtradhārīṃ pūrṇendusundaramukhīṃ madavihvalāṅgīm
children.translated_text: Even now I remember her, the stage-manager of the dance of lovemaking, with a face beautiful as the full moon and limbs bewildered by passion,

children.text: tanvīṃ viśālajaghanastanabhāranamrāṃ vyālolakuntalakalāpavatīṃ smarāmi ||
children.translated_text: slender, bent by the weight of her broad hips and breasts, and bearing a mass of tossing curls.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ masṛṇacandanapaṅkamiśrakastūrikāparimalotthavisarpigandhām
children.translated_text: Even now, on the bed, I remember her whose fragrance spread forth from musk perfume mixed with smooth sandal paste,

children.text: anyonyacañcupuṭacumbanalagnapakṣmayugmābhirāmanayanāṃ śayane smarāmi ||
children.translated_text: whose lovely eyes had pairs of eyelashes joined by the kissing of our two beak-like mouths.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ nidhuvane madhupānaraktām līlādharāṃ kṛśatanuṃ capalāyatākṣīm
children.translated_text: Even now I remember her in lovemaking, flushed by drinking wine, playful-lipped, slender-bodied, with long restless eyes,

children.text: kāśmīrapaṅkamṛganābhikṛtāṅgarāgāṃ karpūrapūgaparipūrṇamukhīṃ smarāmi ||
children.translated_text: her limbs colored with saffron paste and musk, her mouth filled with camphor and betel nut.

children.text: adyāpi tat kanakagaurakṛtāṅgarāgaṃ prasvedabinduvitataṃ vadanaṃ priyāyāḥ
children.translated_text: Even now at the end I remember that face of my beloved, golden-fair and adorned with cosmetics, spread with drops of sweat,

children.text: ante smarāmi ratikhedavilolanetraṃ rāhūparāgaparimuktam ivendubimbam ||
children.translated_text: its eyes wavering from the fatigue of love, like the disk of the moon released from <s>Rāhu</s>'s eclipse.

children.text: adyāpi tanmanasi samparivartate me rātrau mayi kṣutavati kṣitipālaputryā
children.translated_text: Even now this turns about in my mind: at night, when I had sneezed, the king's daughter,

children.text: jīveti maṅgalavacaḥ parihṛtya kopāt karṇe kṛtaṃ kanakapatram anālapantyā ||
children.translated_text: angrily leaving aside the auspicious words 'may you live,' put her golden earring to her ear and did not speak.

children.text: adyāpi tat kanakakuṇḍalaghṛṣṭagaṇḍam āsyaṃ smarāmi viparītaratābhiyoge
children.translated_text: Even now I remember my beloved's face, its cheeks rubbed by golden earrings, during the exertion of reversed lovemaking,

children.text: āndolanaśramajalasphuṭasāndrabindu muktāphalaprakaravicchuritaṃ priyāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: speckled with clusters of pearl-like dense drops of sweat produced by the labor of swaying.

children.text: adyāpi tatpraṇayabhaṅgagurudṛṣṭipātaṃ tasyāḥ smarāmi rativibhramagātrabhaṅgam
children.translated_text: Even now I remember her heavy glance at the breaking of affection, the bending of her body in the play of love,

children.text: vastrāñcalaskhalatacārupayodharāntaṃ dantacchadaṃ daśanakhaṇḍanamaṇḍanaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: the lovely edge of her breast as the hem of her garment slipped, and her lip adorned by the marks of teeth.

children.text: adyāpy aśokanavapallavaraktahastāṃ muktāphalapracayacumbitacūcukāgrām
children.translated_text: Even now inwardly I remember her, her hands red like new aśoka shoots, the tips of her nipples kissed by clusters of pearls,

children.text: antaḥ smitocchvasitapāṇḍuragaṇḍabhittiṃ tāṃ vallabhāmalasahaṃsagatiṃ smarāmi ||
children.translated_text: the surface of her cheeks pale with the breath of a hidden smile, stainless and moving with the gait of a swan.

children.text: adyāpi tat kanakareṇughanorudeśe nyastaṃ smarāmi nakharakṣatalakṣma tasyāḥ
children.translated_text: Even now I remember the mark of a nail-scratch placed on her region of dense golden-powdered thighs,

children.text: ākṛṣṭahemarucirāmbaram utthitāyā lajjāvaśāt karaghṛtaṃ ca tato vrajantyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then, as she rose and went away in the power of shame, her hand holding her golden-bright garment that had been pulled away.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ vidhṛtakajjalalolanetrāṃ pṛthvīṃ prabhūtakusumākulakeśapāśām
children.translated_text: Even now in secret I remember her, her eyes restless and darkened with collyrium, broad, with a mass of hair crowded by abundant flowers,

children.text: sindūrasaṃlulitamauktikadantakāntim ābaddhahemakaṭakāṃ rahasi smarāmi ||
children.translated_text: her pearl-like teeth brightened by vermilion, and golden bracelets fastened on her arms.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ galitabandhanakeśapāśāṃ srastasrajaṃ smitasudhāmadhurādharauṣṭhīm
children.translated_text: Even now in secret I remember her, her mass of hair loosened from its binding, her garland fallen, her lower lip sweet with the nectar of a smile,

children.text: pīnonnatastanayugoparicārucumbanmuktāvalīṃ rahasi loladṛśam smarāmi ||
children.translated_text: with a lovely pearl necklace kissing the tops of her two full, raised breasts, and with darting eyes.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ dhavalaveśmani ratnadīpamālāmayūkhapaṭalair dalitāndhakāre
children.translated_text: Even now I think of her in the white mansion, where darkness was split by arrays of rays from rows of jeweled lamps,

children.text: prāptodyame rahasi saṃmukhadarśanārthaṃ lajjābhayārthanayanām anucintayāmi ||
children.translated_text: when she had set out for a secret face-to-face meeting, her eyes pleading from modesty and fear.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ virahavahninipīḍitāṅgīṃ tanvīṃ kuraṅganayanāṃ surataikapātrīm
children.translated_text: Even now I remember her, her limbs oppressed by the fire of separation, slender, doe-eyed, the sole vessel of lovemaking,

children.text: nānāvicitrakṛtamaṇḍanam āvahantīṃ tāṃ rājahaṃsagamanāṃ sudatīṃ smarāmi ||
children.translated_text: bearing many varied ornaments, that woman with a royal-swan gait and beautiful teeth.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ vihasitāṃ kucabhāranamrāṃ muktākalāpadhavalīkṛtakaṇṭhadeśām
children.translated_text: Even now I remember her smiling, bent by the weight of her breasts, the region of her neck whitened by strings of pearls,

children.text: tat kelimandaragirau kusumāyudhasya kāntāṃ smarāmi rucirojjvalapuṣpaketum ||
children.translated_text: the beloved of the flower-weaponed god upon that play-mountain of pleasure, herself a lovely and radiant flower-banner.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ cāṭuśatadurlalitocitārthaṃ tasyāḥ smarāmi surataklamavihvalāyāḥ
children.translated_text: Even now I remember the speech of my beloved, suitable for the meaning of a hundred flatteries, as she was bewildered by the fatigue of lovemaking,

children.text: avyaktaniḥsvanitakātarakathyamānasaṃkīrṇavarṇaruciraṃ vacanaṃ priyāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: beautiful with mingled syllables, uttered anxiously in indistinct low sounds.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ surataghūrṇanimīlitākṣīṃ srastāṅgayaṣṭigalitāṃśukakeśapāśām
children.translated_text: Even now I think of her, her eyes closed from the dizziness of lovemaking, her slender body slack, her garment and hair loosened and fallen,

children.text: śṛṅgāravāriruhakānanarājahaṃsīṃ janmāntare 'pi nidhane 'py anucintayāmi ||
children.translated_text: the royal swan in the lotus-forest of passion, even in another birth, even at death.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ praṇayinīṃ mṛgaśāvakākṣīṃ pīyūṣapūrṇakucakumbhayugaṃ vahantīm
children.translated_text: Even now, if I should again see that loving woman at the end of the day, doe-fawn-eyed, bearing a pair of nectar-filled breast-jars,

children.text: paśyāmy ahaṃ yadi punar divasāvasāne svargāpavarganararājasukhaṃ tyajāmi ||
children.translated_text: I would abandon the happiness of heaven, liberation, and lordship over men.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ kṣititale varakāminīnāṃ sarvāṅgasundaratayā prathamaikarekhām
children.translated_text: Even now I remember that beloved, the foremost single line among excellent women on earth in the beauty of all her limbs,

children.text: śṛṅgāranāṭakarasottamapānapātrīṃ kāntāṃ smarāmi kusumāyudhabāṇakhinnām ||
children.translated_text: a vessel for drinking the finest rasa of the drama of passion, distressed by the arrows of the flower-weaponed god.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ stimitavastram ivāṅgalagnāṃ prauḍhapratāpamadanānalataptadeham
children.translated_text: Even now I do not forget her for a moment: clinging to my body like a motionless garment, her body heated by the fire of mature, blazing passion,

children.text: bālām anāthaśaraṇām anukampanīyāṃ prāṇādhikāṃ kṣaṇam ahaṃ na hi vismarāmi ||
children.translated_text: a young girl, without refuge or protector, worthy of compassion, dearer than my own life.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ prathamato varasundarīṇāṃ snehaikapātraghaṭitām avanīśaputrīm
children.translated_text: Even now I think of her, foremost among excellent beauties, the daughter of a king, formed as the one vessel of affection:

children.text: haṃhojanā mama viyogahutāśano 'yaṃ soḍhuṃ na śakyateti praticintayāmi ||
children.translated_text: "Ah, people, this fire of separation from me cannot be endured."

children.text: adyāpi vismayakarīṃ tridaśān vihāya buddhir balāc calati me kim ahaṃ karomi
children.translated_text: Even now my mind, astonishingly, abandons the gods and moves by force toward her. What am I to do?

children.text: jānann api pratimuhūrtam ihāntakāle kānteti vallabhatareti mameti dhīrā ||
children.translated_text: Although I know at every moment that this is the time of death, my thought remains firm: "She is my beloved, she is most dear, she is mine."

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ gamanam ity uditaṃ madīyaṃ śrutvaiva bhīruhariṇīm iva cañcalākṣīm
children.translated_text: Even now, when she merely heard that I had said, "I am going," I picture her, with eyes trembling like those of a frightened doe,

children.text: vācaḥ skhaladvigaladāśrujalākulākṣīṃ saṃcintayāmi guruśokavinamravaktrām ||
children.translated_text: her speech faltering, her eyes confused with streams of falling tears, her face bent down under heavy grief.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ sunipuṇaṃ yatatā mayāpi dṛṣṭaṃ na yat sadṛśatovadanaṃ kadācit
children.translated_text: Even now I remember the beloved whose face, though I have searched with the greatest skill, I have never seen equalled anywhere:

children.text: saundaryanirjitarati dvijarājakānti kāntām ihātivimalatvamahāguṇena ||
children.translated_text: one who conquered <s>Rati</s> in beauty and the moon in radiance, through the great quality of her exceeding purity.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ kṣaṇaviyogaviṣopameyāṃ saṅge punar bahutarām amṛtābhiṣekām
children.translated_text: Even now I remember her, for whom a moment's separation was like poison, while union was far more an anointing with nectar:

children.text: tāṃ jīvadhāraṇakarīṃ madanātapatrām udvattakeśanivahāṃ sudatīṃ smarāmi ||
children.translated_text: that fair-toothed woman, sustaining my life, a parasol against the heat of love, with her mass of hair tossed upward.

children.text: adyāpi vāsagṛhato mayi nīyamāne durvārabhīṣaṇakarair yamadūtakalpaiḥ
children.translated_text: Even now, as I was being led from the chamber of love by men dreadful and irresistible, like messengers of <s>Yama</s>,

children.text: kiṃ kiṃ tayā bahuvidhaṃ na kṛtaṃ madarthe vaktuṃ na pāryateti vyathate mano me ||
children.translated_text: my mind is pained: what many things did she not do for my sake? It cannot be fully told.

children.text: adyāpi me niśi divāṭṝhṛdayaṃ dunoti pūrṇendusundaramukhaṃ mama vallabhāyāḥ
children.translated_text: Even now, night and day, the full-moon-beautiful face of my beloved torments my heart,

children.text: lāvaṇyanirjitaratikṣatikāmadarpaṃ bhūyaḥ puraḥ pratipadaṃ na vilokyate yat ||
children.translated_text: because, having conquered the pride of <s>Rati</s> and love through its loveliness, it is no longer seen before me at every step.

children.text: adyāpi tām avahitāṃ manasācalena saṃcintayāmi yuvatīṃ mama jīvitāśām
children.translated_text: Even now, with an unwavering mind, I contemplate that young woman, the hope of my life,

children.text: nānyopabhuktanavayauvanabhārasārāṃ janmāntare 'pi mama saiva gatir yathā syāt ||
children.translated_text: whose fresh youth had not been enjoyed by another, rich with its full burden; may she alone be my refuge even in another birth.

children.text: adyāpi tadvadanapaṅkajagandhalubdhabhrāmyaddvirephacayacumbitagaṇḍadeśām
children.translated_text: Even now my mind utterly swoons at the jingling of the bracelets on her hand-sprouts, playfully shaken,

children.text: līlāvadhūtakarapallavakaṅkaṇānāṃ kvāṇo vimūrchati manaḥ sutarāṃ madīyam ||
children.translated_text: as bees, greedy for the fragrance of her lotus-face, wandered about and kissed the region of her cheeks.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ nakhapadaṃ stanamaṇḍale yad dattaṃ mayāsyamadhupānavimohitena
children.translated_text: Even now I remember the nail-mark that I, bewildered by drinking the honey of her mouth, placed on the circle of her breasts,

children.text: udbhinnaromapulakair bahubhiḥ samantāj jāgarti rakṣati vilokayati smarāmi ||
children.translated_text: while many bristling eruptions of horripilation rose all around, awakening, guarding, and gazing at it.

children.text: adyāpi kopavimukhīkṛtagantukāmā noktaṃ vacaḥ pratidadāti yadaiva vaktram
children.translated_text: Even now I remember: when, turned away in anger and wishing to go, she does not answer a word with her face,

children.text: cumbāmi roditi bhṛśaṃ patito 'smi pāde dāsas tava priyatame bhaja maṃ smarāmi ||
children.translated_text: I kiss her; she weeps violently; fallen at her feet, I say, "I am your servant, dearest, love me."

children.text: adyāpi dhavati manaḥ kim ahaṃ karomi sārdhaṃ sakhībhir api vāsagṛhaṃ sukānte
children.translated_text: Even now my mind runs there. What am I to do? May my time pass with my fair beloved in the chamber of love, together with her friends,

children.text: kāntāṅgasaṃgaparihāsavicitranṛtye krīḍābhirāmeti yātu madīyakālaḥ ||
children.translated_text: delighting in play, in varied dances of embraces, contact with the beloved's limbs, and jesting.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ jagati varṇayituṃ na kaścicchaknoty adṛṣṭasadṛśīṃ ca parigrahaṃ me
children.translated_text: Even now no one in the world is able to describe her, my possession, whose equal has not been seen.

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ tayoḥ sadṛśayoḥ khalu yena rūpaṃ śakto bhaved yadi saiva naro na cānyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Only one who had seen the beauty of the two of them, so alike, could be capable of it, and that very person, no other.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ na khalu vedmi kim īśapatnī śāpaṃ gatā surapater atha kṛṣṇalakṣmī
children.translated_text: Even now I do not know whether she is the wife of a lord fallen under a curse, or the fortune of dark <s>Viṣṇu</s>, or of the lord of the gods,

children.text: dhātraiva kiṃ nu jagataḥ parimohanāya sā nirmitā yuvatiratnadidṛkṣayāṭṝvā ||
children.translated_text: or whether she was created by the Creator himself to bewilder the world, out of a desire to behold the jewel of young women.

children.text: adyāpi tannayanakajjalam ujjvalāsyaṃ viśrāntakarṇayugalaṃ parihāsahetoḥ
children.translated_text: Even now, for the sake of jest, I see her eye-blackening collyrium, her bright face, and the pair of her ears at rest,

children.text: paśye tavātmani navīnapayodharābhyāṃ kṣīṇāṃ vapur yadi vinaśyati no na doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and I say, "If your body, thinned by these newly risen breasts, wastes away in itself, there is no fault in us."

children.text: adyāpi nirmalaśaracchaśigaurakānti ceto muner api haret kim utāsmadīyam
children.translated_text: Even now that face, pure as the autumn moon in spotless radiance, would steal even a sage's mind; what then of mine?

children.text: vaktraṃ sudhāmayam ahaṃ yadi tat prapadye cumban pibāmy avirataṃ vyadhate mano me ||
children.translated_text: If I reach that nectar-filled face and drink it with kisses without cease, my mind is still afflicted.

children.text: adyāpi tat kamalareṇusugandhagandhi tatpremavāri makaradhvajapātakāri
children.translated_text: Even now, if I again obtain that single sacred ford of lovemaking, fragrant with the scent of lotus pollen and with love-water deadly to <s>Makara-dhvaja</s>,

children.text: prāpnomy ahaṃ yadi punaḥ surataikatīrthaṃ prāṇāṃs tyajāmi niyataṃ tadavāptihetoḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall certainly give up my life for the sake of obtaining it.

children.text: adyāpy aho jagati sundaralakṣapūrṇe 'nyānyam uttamaguṇādhikasamprapanne
children.translated_text: Even now, ah, though the world is filled with hundreds of thousands of beauties, each endowed with ever greater excellent qualities,

children.text: anyābhir apy upamituṃ na mayā ca śakyaṃ rūpaṃ tadīyam iti me hṛdaye vitarkaḥ ||
children.translated_text: my doubt in my heart is that I cannot compare her beauty even with any of the others.

children.text: adyāpi sā mama manastaṭinī sadāste romāñcavīcivilasadvipulasvabhāvā
children.translated_text: Even now she always dwells as the riverbank of my mind, with a vast nature gleaming with waves of horripilation,

children.text: kādambakeśararuciḥ kṣatavīkṣaṇaṃ māṃ gātraklamaṃ kathayatī priyarājahaṃsī ||
children.translated_text: my dear royal swan, with the luster of kadamba filaments, telling by her wounded glance of my bodily exhaustion.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ nṛpatī śekhararājaputrīṃ sampūrṇayauvanamadālasaghūrṇanetrīm
children.translated_text: Even now I contemplate her, the crest-jewel among princes' daughters, her eyes reeling languidly with the intoxication of full youth,

children.text: gandharvayakṣasurakiṃnaranāgakanyāṃ svargād aho nipatitām iva cintayāmi ||
children.translated_text: as if she were a daughter of <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, gods, <s>Kiṃnaras</s>, and <s>Nāgas</s>, fallen from heaven.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ nijavapuḥkṛśavedimadhyām uttuṅgasaṃbhṛtasudhāstanakumbhayugmām
children.translated_text: Even now, night and day, I do not forget her: her own body thin at the waist like a slender altar, with a pair of lofty, full, nectar-filled jar-like breasts,

children.text: nānāvicitrakṛtamaṇḍamaṇḍitāṅgī suptotthitāṃ niśi divā na hi vismarāmi ||
children.translated_text: her limbs adorned with many varied ornaments, as she rose from sleep.

children.text: adyāpi tāṃ kanakakāntimadālasāṅgīṃ vrīḍotsukāṃ nipatitām iva ceṣṭamānām
children.translated_text: Even now I remember that woman, like the medicine of life: golden in radiance, her limbs languid with passion, eager with modesty, moving as if fallen down,

children.text: agāṃgasaṃgaparicumbanajātamohāṃ tāṃ jīvanauṣadhim iva pramadāṃ smarāmi ||
children.translated_text: bewildered by embraces of limb with limb and kisses.

children.text: adyāpi tatsuratakelinirastrayuddhaṃ bandhopabandhapatanotthitaśūnyahastam
children.translated_text: Even now I remember that weaponless battle of amorous sport, with tying and counter-tying, with falling and rising, and with hands left empty.

children.text: dantauṣṭhapīḍananakhakṣataraktasiktaṃ tasyāḥ smarāmi ratibandhuraniṣṭhuratvam ||
children.translated_text: I remember her harshness in love, lovely in passion, sprinkled with blood from wounds made by teeth pressing the lips and by nails.

children.text: adyāpy ahaṃ varavadhūsuratopabhogaṃ jīvāmi nānyavidhināṭṝkṣaṇam antareṇa
children.translated_text: Even now I live on the enjoyment of lovemaking with that excellent young bride; by no other means can I pass even a moment.

children.text: tad bhrātaro maraṇam eva hi duḥkhaśāntyai vijñāpayāmi bhavatas tvaritaṃ lunīdhvam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, brothers, indeed for the calming of my sorrow there is only death; I petition you, cut me down quickly.

children.text: adyāpi nojhati haraḥ kila kālakūṭaṃ kūrmo bibharti dharaṇīṃ khalu pṛṣṭhabhāge
children.translated_text: Even now <s>Hara</s>, they say, does not give up the <s>kālakūṭa</s> poison; the tortoise indeed bears the earth on its back.

children.text: ambhonidhir vahati duḥsahavaḍavāgnim aṅgīkṛtaṃ sukṛtinaḥ paripālayanti ||
children.translated_text: The ocean carries the unbearable submarine fire; the virtuous preserve what they have accepted.
